title: Cryptographic dependency risk assessment and staged upgrade plan
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Several runtime services depend on older cryptographic stacks (OpenSSL 1.1.x, legacy JOSE/JWT libraries, and an out-of-date SAML adapter) that expose potential CVE risk and make it difficult to enable modern TLS ciphers, FIPS builds, and safer key handling. We need a low-risk, auditable plan to assess the attack surface, perform compatibility testing, and rollout upgrades with minimal customer impact.

Scope: inventory all services that link OpenSSL or ship bundled crypto; enumerate JWT/OAuth libraries used by public and internal client libraries; locate SAML adapters in auth gateway and legacy enterprise onboarding; produce compatibility matrix and staged upgrade plan. Includes benchmarking to detect perf regressions and runtime memory/latency impacts.

Out of scope: rewriting application auth flows or removing SAML support entirely. This ticket focuses on dependency upgrades, adaptation shims where needed, and rollout strategy with feature flags/canaries.
acceptance_criteria: Complete inventory of services and libraries with current versions and link type (dynamic/static)
Compatibility matrix indicating breaking changes and migration notes for each component
Automated test matrix (unit + e2e) that covers token validation across core flows
Benchmarks demonstrating <=5% median p50 token-generation latency regression on runtime after upgrades or documented mitigation plan
Canary rollout plan with kill-switch and rollback steps validated in staging and small Dedicated pools
Security review sign-off from Security team and verification in internal SBOM and SCA tooling
milestones: M2: Compatibility tests and small migration shims implemented (2026-03-12)
M3: CI matrix expanded, perf baselines collected (2026-03-22)
M4: Staged canary rollout to Dedicated pool alpha then beta (2026-04-05)
M5: Full rollout and SBOM update (2026-04-15)
test_plan: Expand CI to run token validation vectors across OpenSSL 1.1.x, OpenSSL 3.1.x, and BoringSSL-compatible builds
Add synthetic load tests for token issuance path at p50/p95/p99 latencies
Run SAML assertion validation regression suite against updated XML parsers
Include memory leak detection in long-run stress tests for runtime linking changes
rollback_plan: Abort canary and automatically route API traffic back to previous model variants via smart-routing policy
Hotfix: reintroduce compatibility shim in the adapter and redeploy to canary nodes
If rollback fails, escalate to on-call runtime lead and open incident with rollback timeline
